notes:
Source is Cisco's own official data sheet (doc #C78-744227-04, printed 09/23, "Cisco Room Navigator for Table"), retrieved via a third-party mirror (ipphone-warehouse.com) because direct fetches to cisco.com and webex.com returned HTTP 403 in this session. Content matches Cisco/Webex's published Table-stand Room Navigator datasheet.

Physical Interfaces section of the datasheet lists exactly three items: "1x Ethernet (RJ-45) 100/1000 Mbps for LAN (external network) or direct pairing", "1x microUSB (service port)", and "1x factory reset pinhole." The reset pinhole is a mechanical recessed button, not a signal/power connector, so it is excluded from the ports list above.

The device is a 10.1" touch-panel room/booking controller (part number CS-T10-TS-L-K9=, "First Light" table-stand SKU) — it has no HDMI, video, or analog audio I/O; it is not a video source or sink, only a control/UI surface that pairs with a Cisco Room Kit/Room/Board-series codec over Ethernet.

Power is PoE-only (802.3af Class 0, delivered over the RJ-45 jack); no local AC/DC power port exists on the unit itself.

Cisco also sells a "Room Navigator for Wall" variant (same product family, CM-1262 wall-mount data sheet) which differs primarily in mounting hardware (wall bracket vs. detachable table foot stand). I could not independently fetch/confirm the wall-mount datasheet in this session (blocked/404 on the sources tried), so this spec reflects the table-stand variant; treat the wall variant's I/O as very likely identical (same internal board) but unconfirmed. Desktop/wall-mounted accessory device — no rack units.

ports.name: Ethernet (RJ-45)
ports.note: 100/1000 Mbps LAN port for direct or remote pairing to a Cisco video codec; also delivers power via PoE 802.3af Class 0. This is the device's only power connection — there is no separate AC or DC power input.

ports.name: microUSB (service port)
ports.note: Service/debug port; no USB speed grade published in the datasheet.
